lem-emg-potential-maxwell-wave-identity:
## Statement

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be an oriented, time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ with the metric-selected connection $\nabla$ of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Use the curvature operator, Ricci contraction, and sign convention of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. For a real $C^3$ one-form $A$, define $(\Box A)_b:=g^{ac}\nabla_a\nabla_c A_b$, $(\operatorname{div}A):=\nabla^aA_a$, and $(PA)_b:=\Box A_b-\operatorname{Ric}_b{}^cA_c$. Then

$$ \nabla^a(dA)_{ab}=(PA)_b-\nabla_b(\operatorname{div}A). $$

The same identity holds for a complex one-form after complex-linear extension. The identity is local and uses no field equation, gauge condition, boundary condition, or physical assumption.
lem-emg-controlled-maxwell-wkb:
## Statement

Use the smooth oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, metric, connection, curvature sign, length-coordinate SI convention and constants of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open. Let $\theta\in C^4(U,\mathbb R)$ be dimensionless, set $k:=d\theta$, and assume that $k$ is nowhere zero and $g^{-1}(k,k)=0$. Let $a_0,a_1\in C^3(U;T^*M\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C)$; this means that the real and imaginary parts of their coefficients are $C^3$ in every smooth chart. Complex tensor operations and $\nabla$ are extended componentwise and complex-linearly. Define

$$ (\Box a)_b:=g^{ac}\nabla_a\nabla_c a_b,\qquad (Pa)_b:=(\Box a)_b-\operatorname{Ric}_b{}^c a_c,\qquad d_1:=\nabla^a(a_1)_a, $$

and define the first-order operator

$$ (La)_b:=2k^c\nabla_c a_b+(\nabla_c k^c)a_b. $$

Assume pointwise on $U$ that

$$ g^{-1}(k,a_0)=0,\qquad La_0=0,\qquad iLa_1+Pa_0=0,\qquad ik^a(a_1)_a+\nabla^a(a_0)_a=0. $$

These are finite-order ansatz constraints; they assert neither initial data nor a global solution of the transport equations. For $0<\epsilon\le1$, set

$$ A_\epsilon:=\epsilon e^{i\theta/\epsilon}(a_0+\epsilon a_1),\qquad F_\epsilon:=dA_\epsilon. $$

Then $dF_\epsilon=0$ and the exact Maxwell divergence residual is

$$ \nabla^a(F_\epsilon)_{ab} =e^{i\theta/\epsilon}\left[-i\epsilon k_b d_1+ \epsilon^2\bigl((Pa_1)_b-\nabla_b d_1\bigr)\right]. $$

The field-strength expansion is also exact:

$$ F_\epsilon=e^{i\theta/\epsilon}\left[ik\wedge a_0+ \epsilon(da_0+ik\wedge a_1)+\epsilon^2da_1\right]. $$

For units, take $[k]=\mathrm m^{-1}$, $[a_0]=[a_1]=\mathrm{T\,m}$, $[d_1]=\mathrm T$, $[Pa_1]=[\nabla d_1]=\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$, and $[\epsilon]=[\theta]=1$. In one chart and for a compact coordinate set $K$, define

$$ \|S\|_{\infty,K}:= \begin{cases} \max_I\max_{x\in K}|S_I(x)|,&K\ne\varnothing,\\ 0,&K=\varnothing, \end{cases} $$

where $I$ ranges over the finitely many components of the real or complex tensor in that chart. If $K\ne\varnothing$ and finite constants $K_0,D_0,C_0,B_0,B_1\ge0$ satisfy

$$ \|k\|_{\infty,K}\le K_0,\quad \|d_1\|_{\infty,K}\le D_0,\quad \|Pa_1-\nabla d_1\|_{\infty,K}\le C_0,\quad \|da_0+ik\wedge a_1\|_{\infty,K}\le B_0,\quad \|da_1\|_{\infty,K}\le B_1, $$

then

$$ \|\nabla^a(F_\epsilon)_{ab}\|_{\infty,K} \le\epsilon K_0D_0+\epsilon^2C_0,\qquad \|F_\epsilon-e^{i\theta/\epsilon}ik\wedge a_0\|_{\infty,K} \le\epsilon B_0+\epsilon^2B_1. $$

Taking real parts gives real potentials and fields with the same bounds. Every local integral curve of $k^\sharp$ is an affinely parametrized null geodesic and lies in a level set of $\theta$. Along each such ray, a nonzero scalar transport amplitude

$$ \mathcal A(\lambda)=\mathcal A(\lambda_0) \exp\left(-\frac12\int_{\lambda_0}^{\lambda}(\nabla_c k^c)(\gamma(s))\,ds\right) $$

is defined on every compact subinterval of the ray. The one-form $e:=a_0/\mathcal A$ is transverse and parallel transported. At each point the leading polarization is the class $[a_0]\in k^\perp/\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{k\}$, where $k^\perp=\{a:g^{-1}(k,a)=0\}$. This quotient is a two-dimensional complex vector space with a positive induced Hermitian form, and $a_0\mapsto a_0+\beta k$ leaves $k\wedge a_0$ unchanged. If $a_0$ is proportional to $k$, the leading field vanishes. No convergence of a WKB series, existence of amplitudes satisfying the constraints, exact-solution error estimate, or behavior through caustics is asserted.
lem-emg-source-and-test-scaling:
## Statement

Use the field, stress, matter, unit and curvature conventions of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open, let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be constant, and define the Einstein residual for the source-free field model by

$$ \mathscr R_{ab}(g,F;\Lambda):=G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}-\kappa T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}(g,F). $$

Suppose $G_{ab}(g)+\Lambda g_{ab}=0$ on $U$, and let $F_0$ be a smooth real two-form with $dF_0=0$ and $d(\star_gF_0)=0$. For every real dimensionless $\delta$, the field $F_\delta:=\delta F_0$ obeys the same source-free Maxwell equations and

$$ \mathscr R_{ab}(g,F_\delta;\Lambda)=-\kappa\delta^2 T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}(g,F_0). $$

This is an exact residual identity on the fixed metric. If $\delta\ne0$ and $F_0$ is nonzero at a point, its observer energy there is positive and the residual is nonzero there; this does not estimate the distance to a different coupled solution.

Separately, let $\rho,\sigma\in C^1(\Omega)$ and a $C^2$ future timelike field $U$ with $g(U,U)=-c^2$ define charged dust on an open $\Omega\subseteq U$, with $\rho>0$, $T_m^{ab}=\rho U^aU^b$, $j^a=\sigma U^a$, and the formal matter-exchange equation of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. For any dimensionless $\eta>0$, replacing $(\rho,\sigma)$ by $(\eta\rho,\eta\sigma)$ multiplies $T_m$ and $j$ by $\eta$, leaves $\alpha=\sigma/\rho$ unchanged, and leaves the dust acceleration equation $\rho U^a\nabla_aU^b=\sigma F^b{}_cU^c$ unchanged when the prescribed $F$ and $U$ are held fixed. The sourced Maxwell equation must still match the changed current. If both $F$ and $j$ are scaled by $\eta$, Maxwell's equations remain linear but the electromagnetic stress scales by $\eta^2$, whereas the dust stress scales by $\eta$; no general coupled-solution family follows.

For a flat background with $\Lambda=0$ and $T_m=0$, a nonzero source-free Maxwell field cannot solve the exact Einstein equation with the unchanged Minkowski metric, because its observer energy density is positive somewhere.

Finally, in Minkowski space consider only the prescribed Coulomb profile on the finite annulus $\mathcal A_\ell:=\{\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3:\ell<|\mathbf x|<2\ell\}$, where $\ell>0$ is a length, $Q\ne0$ is a charge, $r:=|\mathbf x|$, $\mathbf e_r:=\mathbf x/r$, $\mathbf E(\mathbf x)=Q(4\pi\varepsilon_0r^2)^{-1}\mathbf e_r$, and $\mathbf B=0$. Its Maxwell energy on that annulus is

$$ \mathcal E_\ell=\int_{\mathcal A_\ell}\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}|\mathbf E|^2\,d^3x =\frac{Q^2}{16\pi\varepsilon_0\ell}. $$

Thus this fixed-charge Coulomb cutoff family has diverging shell energy as $\ell\downarrow0$. This finite-annulus calculation asserts no point-source construction, self-field evaluation, or obstruction theorem for arbitrary regularizations.
thm-emg-weak-slow-test-lorentz-limit:
## Statement

Use the mathematical Lorentzian and SI conventions of [[def-emg-matter-formal-systems]]. Fix a length scale $L>0$, a speed $c>0$, a nonzero constant charge-to-mass parameter $\alpha=q/m$, and choose $0<\epsilon\le\epsilon_*\le1$. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $\mathcal K\Subset\Omega$ be a compact convex set. Use length coordinates $x^0=ct$ and $x^i=LX^i$, with $X\in\Omega$ dimensionless. Assume a smooth stationary (independent of $x^0$) Lorentzian metric $g^{(\epsilon)}$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on a neighborhood of $\mathbb R_{x^0}\times L\mathcal K$, with $\partial_0$ chosen future timelike and $t$ increasing along the considered curves, whose components have the form

$$ g_{00}^{(\epsilon)}(X)=-(1+2\epsilon\phi(X))+r_{00}^{(\epsilon)}(X),\qquad g_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}(X)=(1-2\epsilon\phi(X))\delta_{ij}+r_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}(X),\qquad g_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}(X)=r_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}(X). $$

Here $\phi$ is dimensionless and smooth. A spatial multi-index is $\beta=(\beta_1,\beta_2,\beta_3)\in\mathbb N_0^3$, with $|\beta|=\beta_1+\beta_2+\beta_3$ and $\partial_X^\beta:=\partial_{X^1}^{\beta_1}\partial_{X^2}^{\beta_2}\partial_{X^3}^{\beta_3}$. For each such $\beta$ with $|\beta|\le2$, assume the uniform bounds

$$ |\partial_X^\beta r_{00}^{(\epsilon)}|+ \max_{i,j}|\partial_X^\beta r_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}| \le C_g\epsilon^2,\qquad \max_i|\partial_X^\beta r_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}|\le C_g\epsilon^{3/2} $$

on $\mathcal K$, with a fixed finite nonnegative $C_g$. Let $\mathbf e,\mathbf b:\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ be smooth dimensionless fields whose values and first derivatives are bounded on $\mathcal K$. Since $\mathcal K$ is compact, the fixed smooth function $\phi$ and its derivatives used below are also bounded there. Prescribe a smooth stationary (independent of $x^0$) real two-form $F^{(\epsilon)}$ by its Cartesian components

$$ F_{0i}^{(\epsilon)}=-E_i^{(\epsilon)}/c,\qquad F_{ij}^{(\epsilon)}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k^{(\epsilon)},\qquad \alpha\mathbf E^{(\epsilon)}(X)=\frac{\epsilon c^2}{L}\mathbf e(X),\qquad \alpha\mathbf B^{(\epsilon)}(X)=\frac{\sqrt\epsilon\,c}{L}\mathbf b(X). $$

No Maxwell or Einstein equation for this prescribed background field or metric is assumed. Define the dimensionless potential $\phi$ comparison system on $S\in[0,S_*]$ by

$$ \frac{d\mathbf X_N}{dS}=\mathbf W_N,\qquad \frac{d\mathbf W_N}{dS}=-\nabla_X\phi(\mathbf X_N)+\mathbf e(\mathbf X_N)+\mathbf W_N\times\mathbf b(\mathbf X_N), $$

where $(\mathbf u\times\mathbf v)_i:=\sum_{j,k}\epsilon_{ijk}u_jv_k$. Let $f(\mathbf X,\mathbf W)$ denote the six-component right-hand side of this system. Assume that on a compact convex state set $\mathcal Q\subseteq\mathcal K\times\mathbb R^3$, containing both trajectories, its derivative satisfies $\|Df\|_{1\to1}\le L_f$ for a finite nonnegative $L_f$. Here $\|(\mathbf X,\mathbf W)\|_1$ is the sum of the absolute values of its six real components, and $\|Df\|_{1\to1}$ is the operator norm induced by this $\ell^1$ norm.

For each $\epsilon$, let $z_\epsilon$ be a $C^2$ future timelike curve, parameterized by proper time $\tau$ as in [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]], that solves the prescribed external Lorentz equation

$$ \nabla_U U=\alpha F^{(\epsilon)\sharp}(U),\qquad g^{(\epsilon)}(U,U)=-c^2,\qquad U=\frac{dz_\epsilon}{d\tau}. $$

Write its coordinate velocity as $\mathbf w=d\mathbf x/dt$ and assume $|\mathbf w|\le C_v\sqrt\epsilon\,c$ on $[0,S_*]$ for a fixed finite $C_v$. Suppose the relativistic scaled trajectory $(\mathbf X_\epsilon,\mathbf W_\epsilon)$ and the comparison trajectory $(\mathbf X_N,\mathbf W_N)$ exist throughout $[0,S_*]$, remain in $\mathcal Q$, and have the same initial data, where

$$ \mathbf X:=\mathbf x/L,\qquad \mathbf W:=\mathbf w/(\sqrt\epsilon\,c),\qquad S:=\sqrt\epsilon\,ct/L. $$

Then, after choosing $\epsilon_*>0$ sufficiently small in terms of the stated uniform constants, the exact relativistic trajectory satisfies

$$ \frac{d\mathbf X_\epsilon}{dS}=\mathbf W_\epsilon,\qquad \frac{d\mathbf W_\epsilon}{dS} =-\nabla_X\phi(\mathbf X_\epsilon)+\mathbf e(\mathbf X_\epsilon) +\mathbf W_\epsilon\times\mathbf b(\mathbf X_\epsilon)+\mathbf r_\epsilon(S), \qquad \|\mathbf r_\epsilon(S)\|_1\le C_r\epsilon, $$

where $C_r$ depends only on the displayed uniform bounds and the fixed coefficient bounds on $\mathcal K$, and is independent of $\epsilon$. Consequently,

$$ \sup_{0\le S\le S_*}\left(\|\mathbf X_\epsilon(S)-\mathbf X_N(S)\|_1+ \|\mathbf W_\epsilon(S)-\mathbf W_N(S)\|_1\right) \le C_r\epsilon S_*e^{L_fS_*}. $$

The estimate is conditional on existence and common compact containment through the specified finite scaled interval. It does not construct such a long-time family, solve Maxwell's equations for the prescribed fields, or produce a coupled Einstein–Maxwell family. In particular the $\sqrt\epsilon$ magnetic scaling can fail a coupled Einstein stress hierarchy unless additional matter scales are supplied.
